events.summary: At its Investor Day on 6 Oct, Marvell (maker of the signal-processing chips used inside optical transceivers) raised its fiscal 2028 revenue target to about $20bn from about $18bn (consensus about $18.2bn), with data-center revenue near $18bn, and set a $70-90bn fiscal 2031 framework. Reports say the extra ~$2bn comes from scale-out optics, scale-up optics and switching; Marvell said it ships 1.6T optical technologies in volume and is developing 3.2T. Marvell's stock dipped about 3% early, then rallied to close up about 6%. Optical peers (LITE +3.8%, CRDO +3.9%) finished higher while SMH fell 0.2%.
events.why_it_matters: A big supplier to the same AI data-center customers says optical connections are growing faster than it expected, which supports demand for AOI's 800G/1.6T transceivers. It is a sector signal, not AOI news. Marvell's targets come only from tier-3 reports: Marvell's IR page showed no investor-day release when checked (it confirms only the event date).

events.summary: AAOI fell 5.85% to $122.54 on Wednesday (opened -3.1% at $126.12, low $119.73), giving back Tuesday's gain: +0.80% over two days vs Monday's $121.57. why_chain.text: The gain started at the open (gap +3.6%) and was +6% by 9:52 ET while optical peers were flat, so the morning move was AAOI's own.

The only explanation in print (tier 3) is the completed $600m share sale ('clearing known share supply'), but that came out a session earlier. A delayed reaction to the end of the selling is possible but unproven.

Later in the session the optical group rose (LITE +3.8%, CRDO +3.9%, VIAV +2.6%) while SMH fell, on the day Marvell raised its FY2028 target to about $20bn, citing optics. That probably supported AAOI's afternoon and close; the exact timing was not verified.

Basic driver: investors are betting on AI data-center spending on optical links (800G/1.6T modules), amplified by momentum: AAOI is up 29.29% in five sessions with a 1-year beta to the market of 4.26.
Wednesday -5.85%: market -0.39, industry -1.80, company -3.67 (z -0.47, normal noise).
Stocks slipped from records as the 10-year yield hit 5.31% and oil rose, ahead of the Fed minutes; chips and optical peers fell.
Higher yields hurt richly valued, high-beta stocks most, and after a 29% five-day run some profit-taking is typical. No AAOI-specific cause was found; the Form 4 came after the close.

products.name: 800G and 1.6T data-center optical transceivers
products.what_it_is: Plug-in modules that turn a server's or switch's electrical signals into laser light and back, at 800 or 1,600 gigabits per second.
products.analogy: A translator at each end of a phone line: one turns speech (electricity) into a coded signal (light) for the long wire (fibre), the other turns it back.
products.buyers: Large cloud and AI data-center operators, directly or through a distributor. Top 10 customers are 99% of revenue; one distributor owed $211.0m at 30 June (AOI 10-Q, 2026-08-06).
products.how_it_works: A laser chip encodes data as light pulses into fibre; a photodetector at the far end turns them back into electricity; a signal-processing chip (the kind Marvell sells) cleans up the signal.
products.sales: Units not disclosed. Proxy: Q2 2026 data-center revenue $107.662m (+140.4% from $44.791m a year earlier), 56.1% of total revenue of $191.922m; the CEO said 800G volume 'more than doubled sequentially'.
products.stage: 800G ramping in volume. 1.6T: capacity being built; volume shipments not stated in the Q2 release.
products.size_for_company: 56.1% of Q2 2026 revenue (CATV $80.578m was the other big piece, 42.0%).
products.competition: Chinese makers led by Zhongji Innolight (about 27% of the global data-center transceiver market per a tier-3 report), plus Coherent and Lumentum.
products.why_investors_care: The CEO said demand will outpace AOI's production capacity through mid-2027. Capacity was approaching 200,000 units a month in Q2, with a target of about 650,000 800G/1.6T units a month by end-2026, so revenue growth depends on adding capacity.
products.watch_next: Q3 results (about 5 Nov): data-center revenue, the capacity update against 650,000 a month, and gross margin against the 29-30.5% non-GAAP guide.
